title: Hardening console observability after tenant-level capacity surge exposed telemetry gaps
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Summary: During the 2026-03-07 console capacity surge, customer-facing dashboards and alerting failed to surface the tenant-scoped build-up of KV-cache misses and routing throttles. Investigation found three primary telemetry blind spots: (1) several critical tracepoints in the request router and model-variant selection path were sampled out or not instrumented at high-cardinality, (2) a key dashboard query aggregated across tenants (missing tenant_id filter/tag) hiding a single-tenant hot-spot, and (3) the metrics ingestion pipeline dropped high-cardinality metrics at the batching/aggregation layer during sustained bursts. This ticket consolidates remediation action items, owners, rollout plan, and acceptance criteria.
action_items: Add tenant_id and model_variant tags to router tracepoints and KV-cache events (owner: Liam).
Emit new metric: console.kv_cache.miss_ratio with tenant_id and service tags; ensure cardinality controls applied (owner: Priya Gupta).
Create per-tenant heatmap dashboard panels for P50/P95/P99 tail latency and kv_cache miss_ratio (owner: UX/Console dashboard lead: Marco).
Fix dashboard queries that aggregate across tenants; add default tenant filter and explicit aggregation windows (owner: Marco).
Update sampling policy for router traces: increase retention for error and high-latency traces and keep 100% sampling for events with kv_cache.miss=true (owner: Observability infra: Nora Patel).
Add alerting: new SLO-based alert when any tenant shows sustained kv_cache.miss_ratio > 5% for 10 minutes or P99 latency > 500ms (owner: SRE: Daniel O'Connor).
Add ingestion back-pressure telemetry and a telemetry-dropped metric to detect pipeline truncation (owner: Telemetry infra: Chen Wu).
Ship a short runbook: triage steps, how to pivot requests to fallback model variant, and where to find per-tenant heatmaps (owner: Liam).
Canary rollout: enable tenant-level metrics for 10 pilot tenants for 48h, validate dashboards and alert fidelity before global rollout (owner: Product Ops: Samira Khan).
acceptance_criteria: Router traces include tenant_id and model_variant tags in 95% of sampled requests for the canary tenants.
New metric console.kv_cache.miss_ratio ingested and visible in Grafana for canary tenants within 5 minutes of generation.
Per-tenant heatmap panels show distinct tenant lines and are linked from the incident runbook.
Alerts fire in test mode for synthetic tenants when configured thresholds are breached and escalate to SRE pager.
Telemetry ingestion reports no > 1% unexplained drops for canary period (48h).
notes: Root cause sketch: the pipeline's aggressive aggregation heuristic removed low-cardinality tags during high-ingest windows; dashboards then grouped by service only, obfuscating single-tenant hotspots.
Trade-off: adding tenant_id to every metric increases label cardinality. We'll limit global rollout and apply cardinality bucketing; pilot tenants will use full tags.
Privacy note: tenant_id values will be hashed in analytics dashboards; raw tenant identifiers remain available only to SRE in restricted views (see security doc link).
